gallery.filename: Luphou Nung - a historical gravestone kept inside the Kangla fort in Imphal.jpg
gallery.title: File:Luphou Nung - a historical gravestone kept inside the Kangla fort in Imphal.jpg
gallery.description: "Luphou Nung" is a historical gravestone of a Chinese invader, kept inside the Kangla fort in Imphal. A Chinese invader named "Moidana" (or "Mayadana") was defeated and slain by Meitei king Mungyamba of Kangleipak (Manipur) kingdom in 1576 A.D. The invader was crushed and buried under the "Luphou Nung" stone.

gallery.filename: Marong Khong - a sacred water body inside the Kangla Fort in Imphal.jpg
gallery.title: File:Marong Khong - a sacred water body inside the Kangla Fort in Imphal.jpg
gallery.description: Marong Khong is a sacred water body inside the Kangla Fort in Imphal. It is located in the northern side of the tombs of Meitei Kings, Maharaja Narasingh and Maharaja Bodhachandra, and in the southern side of the Rose Garden of the Kangla Palace.

gallery.filename: Manglen of Maharaja Bodhchandra inside the Kangla fort in Imphal.jpg
gallery.title: File:Manglen of Maharaja Bodhchandra inside the Kangla fort in Imphal.jpg
gallery.description: The image shows the Manglen of Maharaja Bodhchandra inside the Kangla fort in Imphal. "Manglen" is the site where kings of Kangleipak (Manipur) were cremated. The mortal remains of Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh (Bodhachandra Singh), the last ruler of sovereign state of Manipur, was consigned to flames at this place on the 9th December, 1955.
